intro: HIPL meets in person: small evenings, walks through living history, hands-on service and student debates. Seva and sabha, side by side.

programmes.name: HIPL Salons
programmes.description: A host, a living room or a café, chai, and one question worth an evening. No speeches, no panels: everyone talks. Salons are the easiest way to bring HIPL to your city.
how: A host picks one question from the 100 Questions or the news.
15–25 people, by invitation and open sign-up.
Two hours, one conversation, a short note afterwards in the Dispatch.

programmes.name: Heritage Walks
programmes.description: Walk through living temples, ghats and old neighbourhoods with a guide who knows the history and the people who keep these places alive. History told on the spot, with sources.
how: A guide (historian, local or priest) plans a two-hour route.
Groups of up to 25, early morning.
Every walk ends with a stop for breakfast and questions.

programmes.name: Culture Nights
programmes.description: An evening of performance and conversation: a raga and the story behind it, a film screening and a discussion, a dancer on how a tradition is reinvented.
how: One artist or performance, one conversation.
Partnered with cultural venues and collectives.

programmes.name: Seva Saturdays
programmes.description: Seva is an idea best understood with your hands. Once a month we volunteer with a local partner, from temple kitchens and ghat clean-ups to reading with children, then talk about what service asks of us.
how: A partner organisation sets the task.
Three hours of work, thirty minutes of conversation.
Open to everyone, of any belief or none.

programmes.name: Campus Circles
programmes.description: Student-run HIPL chapters that host debates, reading circles and Salons on campus, with the Delhi Union as our first debating partner. A starter kit, speakers and a network of other Circles.
how: Three students and a faculty friend can start a Circle.
We send a starter kit, debate formats and speaker contacts.
Circles meet monthly and join an inter-campus debate each term.

programmes.name: Voices
programmes.description: Not everything happens in a room. Pitch an essay, a personal story, a review or a story from your town, and we'll edit it with you and publish it under your name.
